response: Well-differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is not considered clinically early cancer. Research has shown that there is no significant difference in disease-free survival between patients with well-differentiated and less-differentiated HCCs. This suggests that well-differentiated HCCs can still have a similar prognosis to less-differentiated HCCs, and therefore, should not be considered as early cancer. Early detection through methods like ultrasonographic screening can improve the prognosis of patients with HCC, but the differentiation of the tumor itself does not necessarily indicate an early stage of the disease.
